hints.title: Turn intersections into roots of one function
hints.body: Equate the curve heights and rearrange: F(x)=x3+x2−16x+4−k=0. We need three distinct roots, exactly two of them positive.
hints.recap: Intersections of two graphs are zeros of their difference.
hints.pitfall: The parameter shifts the whole cubic vertically; it does not change its derivative.
hints.pause: Differentiate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> and find its stationary inputs.

recall.reminder: Intersections of two graphs are zeros of their difference.

hints.title: Focus on the positive half of the graph
hints.body: F′(x)=(3x+8)(x−2). For x>0, the function decreases to x=2 and then increases. Two distinct positive roots therefore require F(0)>0 and F(2)<0.
hints.recap: Root counting can use turning heights and endpoint signs without solving the cubic.
hints.pitfall: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> would give a root at zero, which is not positive.
hints.pause: Evaluate the two heights in terms of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Evaluate and test the conditions
hints.body: Evaluate the two heights in your sign conditions. Solve the resulting strict inequalities in the parameter, then check the remaining part of the graph.
hints.recap: A repeated root or a root at zero must be treated separately when distinct positive roots are required.
hints.pitfall: Necessary height conditions should also be checked to ensure the required total number of intersections.
hints.pause: Derive the parameter bounds and justify the third distinct root for every parameter you retain.

recall.reminder: A repeated root or a root at zero must be treated separately when distinct positive roots are required.

solution:
Intersections satisfy F(x)=x3+x2−16x+4−k=0, with F′(x)=(3x+8)(x−2).

On x>0, F decreases until x=2 and then increases. It has two distinct positive roots exactly when F(0)=4−k>0 and F(2)=−16−k<0. These give k<4 and k>−16.

For these values, the negative tail and F(0)>0 force a negative root as well. The cubic therefore has exactly the three required distinct roots.

The complete range is −16<k<4: E.
knowledgePattern: Constrain a cubic intercept and positive minimum to control root signs
